name: ZeroQuant-V2: Exploring Post-training Quantization in LLMs from Comprehensive Study to Low Rank Compensation
authors: Lin, Li, Cai, Wu, Zhang, Chen
problem: No systematic study existed of how PTQ choices (scheme, model family, bit width, weight vs activation) interact across the 125M-176B scale range.
mechanism: Two parts: (1) a sensitivity study crossing RTN / GPTQ / ZeroQuant and variants over weight-only, activation-only and weight-and-activation quantization on two model families from 125M to 176B; (2) Low-Rank Compensation (LoRC) - after quantizing to the target bit width, fit a rank-r matrix per transformer block to reconstruct the residual quantization error, adding a small amount of parameters to recover quality.
speedup_reported: Paper's own NEGATIVE result is the headline: across every method tested, 'none of the current methods can achieve the original model quality for quantization with either INT4-weight or INT4-weight-and-INT8-activation'. LoRC is reported as improving quality recovery with a minimal parameter increase, but the abstract does NOT give a headline compression ratio paired with a paired quality delta, so speedup_reported is deliberately not invented here. Sensitivity finding worth keeping: activation quantization is more susceptible than weight quantization, and smaller models often beat larger ones on activation quantization.
